title: Maximum Price to Fill a Bag
summary: Given a 2D integer array items where each item is represented as [pricei, weighti], and a positive integer capacity, you can divide each item into two parts with any ratio such that the sum of the parts equals 1.
statement: Given a 2D integer array items where each item is represented as [pricei, weighti], and a positive integer capacity, you can divide each item into two parts with any ratio such that the sum of the parts equals 1. The weight and price of each part can be calculated as weighti * part1 and pricei * part1 for the first part, and weighti * part2 and pricei * part2 for the second part, where part1 + part2 == 1. Your task is to determine the maximum total price of the items that can fill a bag with the given capacity. If it is impossible to fill the bag with the given items, return -1. The result should be within 10^-5 of the actual maximum total price to be considered correct.
constraints: Each item is [price,weight] and may be divided in any fractional ratio.
Fill exactly capacity units of weight while maximizing total proportional price.
Return -1 when all items together weigh less than capacity; floating answers use tolerance.
hints: Because items are divisible, compare their price per unit of weight.
Consume items from greatest density to smallest, taking a final fraction when necessary.
Stop immediately when capacity reaches zero; return -1 if the sorted items are exhausted first.
Exchanging any lower-density weight for available higher-density weight cannot decrease value, proving the greedy ordering.
editorial: Exchanging any lower-density weight for available higher-density weight cannot decrease value, proving the greedy ordering.
